stories.title: The French Revolution
stories.blurb: How a bankrupt monarchy called a parliament and got a republic, a terror and a general.

steps.name: Estates General of 1789
steps.what: Louis XVI convenes the Estates-General for the first time since 1614 to fix a bankrupt treasury.
steps.why: The deputies of the Third Estate would turn a fiscal meeting into a claim to speak for the nation.
steps.date_note: Wikidata gives 1789-01-24; the study spine uses 1789-05-05 (Wikipedia: Estates General of 1789)

steps.name: Tennis Court Oath
steps.what: Locked out of their hall, the Third Estate swears not to part until France has a constitution.
steps.why: Sovereignty moves, on paper, from the king to the nation.

steps.name: Storming of the Bastille
steps.what: A Paris crowd seizes the royal fortress and its gunpowder.
steps.why: The street enters politics; the king gives way and the revolution spreads to the provinces.

steps.name: Feudalism abolished
steps.what: In one night session the Assembly votes away seigneurial dues, tithes and noble privileges.
steps.why: The legal order of the old regime ends; peasants keep the revolution on their side.

steps.name: Declaration of the Rights of Man
steps.what: The Assembly adopts a declaration of natural rights, equality before the law and popular sovereignty.
steps.why: A text copied by liberal constitutions across Europe for a century.
steps.wikipedia: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

steps.name: Flight to Varennes
steps.what: The royal family is caught fleeing towards the Austrian Netherlands.
steps.why: Trust in a constitutional king collapses; republicanism grows.

steps.name: War of the First Coalition
steps.what: The Legislative Assembly declares war on the Habsburg monarch.
steps.why: Begins 23 years of almost continuous European war.

steps.name: Battle of Valmy
steps.what: A French citizen army turns back the Prussian advance on Paris.
steps.why: The revolution survives; the Republic is proclaimed the next day.

steps.name: Execution of Louis XVI
steps.what: The former king is guillotined on the Place de la Révolution.
steps.why: Every crowned head in Europe is now at war with France.

steps.name: War in the Vendée
steps.what: A Catholic and royalist peasant rising against conscription.
steps.why: Its repression kills perhaps 150,000 people, the revolution against its own provinces.

steps.name: The Terror
steps.what: The Convention makes terror "the order of the day"; the Law of Suspects follows.
steps.why: About 17,000 official executions; the model of revolutionary dictatorship.

steps.name: Thermidor: fall of Robespierre
steps.what: The Convention turns on Robespierre, executed the next day.
steps.why: The Terror ends and the revolution turns conservative.

steps.name: Treaty of Campo Formio
steps.what: Austria cedes Belgium and recognises French puppet republics in Italy; Venice goes to Austria.
steps.why: Bonaparte, not the Directory, now dictates peace.

steps.name: coup of 18 Brumaire
steps.what: Napoleon Bonaparte overthrows the Directory and becomes First Consul.
steps.why: The revolution ends in the rule of one man.

stories.title: Napoleon's Europe
stories.blurb: A continent redrawn by one army: kingdoms invented, the Holy Roman Empire ended, Russia invaded.

steps.name: Battle of Marengo
steps.what: Bonaparte defeats the Austrians in Piedmont.
steps.why: Secures his power at home and northern Italy abroad.

steps.name: Concordat of 1801
steps.what: Napoleon and Pope Pius VII restore the Catholic Church in France under state control.
steps.why: Ends the religious war of the revolution.

steps.name: Napoleonic Code
steps.what: The French Civil Code is promulgated.
steps.why: Exported by conquest, it is still the base of civil law across Europe and Latin America.

steps.name: coronation of Napoleon I
steps.what: Napoleon crowns himself Emperor of the French in Notre-Dame.
steps.why: A new dynasty claims Europe by conquest, not birth.

steps.name: Battle of Trafalgar
steps.what: Nelson destroys the Franco-Spanish fleet.
steps.why: Britain rules the sea for a century; invasion of Britain is off.

steps.name: Battle of Austerlitz
steps.what: Napoleon crushes Austria and Russia in Moravia.
steps.why: The Third Coalition breaks; Austria leaves Germany to France.

steps.name: End of the Holy Roman Empire
steps.what: Francis II abdicates as Holy Roman Emperor after the Confederation of the Rhine is formed.
steps.why: A thousand-year frame for Germany is gone; the German question begins.
steps.wikipedia: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire

steps.name: Battle of Jena–Auerstedt
steps.what: Prussia's army is destroyed in a single day.
steps.why: The shock behind the Prussian reforms of Stein and Scharnhorst.

steps.name: Continental System
steps.what: The Berlin Decree bans British trade with French-controlled Europe.
steps.why: Economic war that pushes Napoleon into Portugal, Spain and Russia.

steps.name: Treaties of Tilsit
steps.what: Napoleon and Alexander I divide Europe on a raft in the Neman.
steps.why: Prussia is halved and a Duchy of Warsaw created.

steps.name: Dos de Mayo Uprising
steps.what: Madrid rises against French troops; mass executions follow.
steps.why: Starts the Peninsular War, the "Spanish ulcer" that bleeds the empire.

steps.name: Battle of Wagram
steps.what: Napoleon beats Austria's second attempt at revenge.
steps.why: Austria allies with France; Napoleon marries Marie Louise.

steps.name: Invasion of Russia
steps.what: The Grande Armée of about 600,000 crosses the Neman.
steps.why: Fewer than a tenth return; the empire's army is broken.

steps.name: Battle of Borodino
steps.what: The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars, outside Moscow.
steps.why: Napoleon takes Moscow but not the war.

steps.name: Battle of Berezina
steps.what: The retreating army escapes across the frozen river at heavy cost.
steps.why: The word for catastrophe in French: c'est la Bérézina.

steps.name: Battle of Leipzig
steps.what: Russia, Prussia, Austria and Sweden defeat Napoleon at Leipzig.
steps.why: The largest battle in Europe before 1914; Germany is lost to France.

steps.name: Treaty of Fontainebleau
steps.what: Napoleon abdicates and is exiled to Elba.
steps.why: The Bourbons return under Louis XVIII.

steps.name: The Hundred Days
steps.what: Napoleon lands from Elba and marches on Paris.
steps.why: One last campaign; the allies declare him an outlaw.

steps.name: Battle of Waterloo
steps.what: Wellington and Blücher defeat Napoleon in Belgium.
steps.why: The end of the wars; Napoleon dies on St Helena in 1821.

stories.title: The Vienna order and its cracks
stories.blurb: Five great powers try to freeze Europe; nations and liberals keep breaking the ice.

steps.name: Congress of Vienna
steps.what: Metternich hosts the powers to redraw the map after Napoleon.
steps.why: Its balance of power keeps the peace among the great powers for 40 years.

steps.name: Final Act of Vienna
steps.what: A German Confederation of 39 states; Prussia gains the Rhineland; Russia most of Poland.
steps.why: The map of 1815 sets every border fight of the century.

steps.name: Holy Alliance
steps.what: Russia, Austria and Prussia pledge to rule as Christian monarchs.
steps.why: The conservative club that intervenes against revolutions.

steps.name: Peterloo Massacre
steps.what: Cavalry charge a reform meeting of 60,000 at St Peter's Field.
steps.why: British radicalism gets its martyrs; reform comes in 1832.

steps.name: Carlsbad Decrees
steps.what: The German Confederation censors the press and polices universities.
steps.why: Metternich's system of repression against nationalism.

steps.name: Greek War of Independence
steps.what: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule in the Peloponnese.
steps.why: The first nation carved from the Ottoman Empire, with great-power help.

steps.name: Decembrist revolt
steps.what: Army officers demand a constitution as Nicholas I takes the throne.
steps.why: Crushed in a day; Nicholas rules as the gendarme of Europe.

steps.name: Battle of Navarino
steps.what: British, French and Russian fleets destroy the Ottoman-Egyptian navy.
steps.why: Makes Greek independence certain.

steps.name: July Revolution
steps.what: Three days of barricades overthrow Charles X; Louis-Philippe becomes king.
steps.why: Signal for revolts in Belgium, Poland and Italy.

steps.name: Belgian Revolution
steps.what: An opera riot in Brussels becomes a revolt against the Dutch king.
steps.why: Belgium is independent and, from 1839, guaranteed neutral, the "scrap of paper" of 1914.

steps.name: November Uprising
steps.what: Polish officers rise against Russian rule.
steps.why: Crushed in 1831; the Great Emigration carries Polish nationalism to Paris.

steps.name: Great Reform Act
steps.what: Britain redistributes seats and widens the franchise.
steps.why: Reform without revolution becomes the British path.

steps.name: Slavery Abolition Act
steps.what: Britain abolishes slavery in most of its empire from 1834.
steps.why: About 800,000 people freed; owners, not the enslaved, are compensated.

steps.name: coronation of Queen Victoria
steps.what: Victoria is crowned in Westminster Abbey.
steps.why: Her reign of 63 years names the age.

steps.name: Great Irish Famine
steps.what: Potato blight destroys the main food of the Irish poor.
steps.why: About a million die and a million emigrate; Ireland's population never recovers.

stories.title: The Revolutions of 1848
stories.blurb: The springtime of peoples: in a few weeks, half of Europe's capitals fall to the barricades.

steps.name: Sicilian revolution of 1848
steps.what: Palermo rises against the Bourbon king of the Two Sicilies.
steps.why: The first of the year's revolutions.

steps.name: The Communist Manifesto
steps.what: Marx and Engels publish their manifesto in London.
steps.why: Little read in 1848; the most influential pamphlet of the next century.

steps.name: French Revolution of 1848
steps.what: Louis-Philippe abdicates; the Second Republic is proclaimed.
steps.why: Brings universal male suffrage to France and sets off Central Europe.

steps.name: Vienna rises; Metternich falls
steps.what: Students and workers storm the streets; Metternich flees to London.
steps.why: The architect of the 1815 order is gone.
steps.wikipedia: Revolutions of 1848 in the Austrian Empire

steps.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
steps.what: Petőfi reads the National Song; the April Laws make Hungary self-governing.
steps.why: Begins a war for independence against the Habsburgs.

steps.name: Barricades in Berlin
steps.what: Street fighting forces Frederick William IV to promise a constitution.
steps.why: Prussia briefly bows to liberalism.

steps.name: Five Days of Milan
steps.what: Milan drives out Radetzky's Austrian garrison.
steps.why: Piedmont declares war on Austria: the First Italian War of Independence.

steps.name: Frankfurt National Assembly
steps.what: An elected all-German assembly meets in St Paul's Church.
steps.why: Writes a liberal constitution for a united Germany that no king will accept.

steps.name: Prague uprising
steps.what: Windischgrätz bombards Prague after a Slav Congress.
steps.why: The first counter-revolutionary victory of the Habsburgs.

steps.name: June Days
steps.what: Paris workers revolt when the national workshops close; the army crushes them.
steps.why: Liberals and workers split; the revolution turns on itself.

steps.name: Louis-Napoleon elected president
steps.what: Napoleon's nephew wins France's first presidential election by a landslide.
steps.why: He makes himself Emperor Napoleon III by 1852.

steps.name: Roman Republic
steps.what: Mazzini and Garibaldi proclaim a republic in Rome; French troops end it in July.
steps.why: Garibaldi's retreat makes him a legend.

steps.name: Frederick William refuses the crown
steps.what: The Prussian king rejects the imperial crown offered by Frankfurt.
steps.why: German unity from below is dead; it will come from Prussia.

steps.name: Surrender at Világos
steps.what: The Hungarian army surrenders to the Russians who came to Austria's aid.
steps.why: The last revolution of 1848 falls; Habsburg rule is restored.

stories.title: Italian unification
stories.blurb: Eight states become one kingdom in thirteen years, by diplomacy, war and a thousand red shirts.

steps.name: Battle of Novara
steps.what: Radetzky crushes Piedmont; Charles Albert abdicates.
steps.why: Victor Emmanuel II keeps Piedmont's constitution, the only one left in Italy.

steps.name: Cavour becomes prime minister
steps.what: Count Cavour leads Piedmont-Sardinia.
steps.why: He builds railways, banks and alliances for unification.

steps.name: Plombières Agreement
steps.what: Cavour and Napoleon III secretly plan a war on Austria.
steps.why: France will help in exchange for Nice and Savoy.

steps.name: Battle of Magenta
steps.what: French and Piedmontese beat Austria west of Milan.
steps.why: Opens Lombardy.

steps.name: Battle of Solferino
steps.what: A huge, bloody battle that wins Lombardy for Piedmont.
steps.why: Henry Dunant saw it and founded the Red Cross.

steps.name: Treaty of Turin
steps.what: Piedmont cedes Nice and Savoy to France; central Italy votes to join.
steps.why: The price and the first harvest of unification.

steps.name: Expedition of the Thousand
steps.what: Garibaldi lands in Sicily with about a thousand volunteers.
steps.why: Topples the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in five months.

steps.name: Meeting at Teano
steps.what: Garibaldi hands the south to Victor Emmanuel.
steps.why: The revolutionary yields to the monarchy.

steps.name: Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
steps.what: Victor Emmanuel II becomes King of Italy.
steps.why: Italy exists; Venice and Rome are still outside it.
steps.wikipedia: Proclamation of the Kingdom of Italy

steps.name: Venetia joins Italy
steps.what: After Prussia beats Austria, Venetia passes to Italy and votes to join.
steps.why: Unification rides on German wars.

steps.name: Capture of Rome
steps.what: Italian troops breach the Porta Pia as French troops leave for their war with Prussia.
steps.why: The Papal States end; Rome becomes the capital in 1871.

stories.title: German unification
stories.blurb: From a customs union to an empire proclaimed in the Hall of Mirrors: "blood and iron".

steps.name: Zollverein
steps.what: The German Customs Union, led by Prussia, comes into force.
steps.why: Economic unity without Austria, a generation before political unity.

steps.name: First German railway
steps.what: The Bavarian Ludwig Railway opens between Nuremberg and Fürth.
steps.why: Railways knit the German market together.

steps.name: "Blood and iron" speech
steps.what: New Prussian minister-president Bismarck tells the Diet that iron and blood, not speeches, decide great questions.
steps.why: Sets the method of German unification.

steps.name: Battle of Dybbøl
steps.what: Prussia storms the Danish lines in Schleswig.
steps.why: Denmark loses Schleswig and Holstein.

steps.name: Battle of Königgrätz
steps.what: Prussia defeats Austria in Bohemia in seven weeks of war.
steps.why: Austria is pushed out of Germany for good.

steps.name: North German Confederation
steps.what: A federal state under Prussia replaces the German Confederation north of the Main.
steps.why: The skeleton of the empire, with a parliament elected by all men.

steps.name: Ems Dispatch
steps.what: Bismarck edits a royal telegram to insult France.
steps.why: France declares war on 19 July, as he wanted.

steps.name: Battle of Sedan
steps.what: Napoleon III and his army surrender to the Prussians.
steps.why: The Second Empire falls; a republic is proclaimed in Paris on 4 September.

steps.name: German Empire proclaimed
steps.what: William I is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors.
steps.why: A new great power at the centre of Europe.

steps.name: Paris Commune
steps.what: Paris rebels against the new French government; it is crushed in the Bloody Week of May.
steps.why: The founding myth of revolutionary socialism.

steps.name: Treaty of Frankfurt
steps.what: France cedes Alsace and most of Lorraine and pays five billion francs.
steps.why: French revanche poisons Franco-German relations until 1914.
steps.date_note: Wikidata gives 1871-11-07; the study spine uses 1871-05-10 (Wikipedia: Treaty of Frankfurt)

stories.title: The Eastern Question
stories.blurb: What happens to the Ottoman lands in Europe as the empire weakens? A century of answers.

steps.name: First Serbian Uprising
steps.what: Serbs under Karađorđe rise against the Janissaries.
steps.why: The start of the Balkan national states.

steps.name: treaty of Adrianople
steps.what: After a Russian advance, the Ottomans accept Greek autonomy and Serbian self-rule.
steps.why: Russia becomes the Balkan Christians' patron.

steps.name: Tanzimat edict
steps.what: The Gülhane edict promises equality and security to all Ottoman subjects.
steps.why: Begins forty years of Ottoman modernising reform.

steps.name: Crimean War
steps.what: The Ottomans declare war on Russia; Britain and France join in 1854.
steps.why: The Vienna order breaks; the first war with telegraphs, railways and war correspondents.

steps.name: Charge of the Light Brigade
steps.what: A misread order sends British cavalry into Russian guns.
steps.why: A poem and a byword for bungled command.

steps.name: Fall of Sevastopol
steps.what: Russia abandons its Black Sea base after an 11-month siege.
steps.why: Defeat pushes Alexander II into reform.

steps.name: Treaty of Paris
steps.what: Ends the Crimean War; the Black Sea is neutralised.
steps.why: Austria isolated, Russia humbled: the ground for Italian and German unification.

steps.name: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia
steps.what: Both principalities elect Alexandru Ioan Cuza, creating Romania.
steps.why: A nation made by electing the same man twice.
steps.wikipedia: United Principalities of Moldavia and Wallachia

steps.name: April Uprising of 1876
steps.what: Bulgarians rise; Ottoman irregulars massacre thousands.
steps.why: The "Bulgarian horrors" turn European opinion.

steps.name: Russo-Turkish War
steps.what: Russia declares war on the Ottoman Empire.
steps.why: Russian armies reach the gates of Istanbul.

steps.name: Siege of Plevna
steps.what: Osman Pasha holds Plevna for five months.
steps.why: The delay gives Europe time to intervene.

steps.name: Treaty of San Stefano
steps.what: Creates a large Bulgaria under Russian influence.
steps.why: Britain and Austria refuse it.

steps.name: congress of Berlin
steps.what: Bismarck hosts the powers to revise San Stefano.
steps.why: The great powers, not the Balkan peoples, decide the Balkan map.

steps.name: Treaty of Berlin of 1878
steps.what: A smaller Bulgaria; Serbia, Montenegro and Romania independent; Austria-Hungary occupies Bosnia.
steps.why: Settles the crisis and plants the next ones.

steps.name: Bosnian annexation crisis
steps.what: Austria-Hungary annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina.
steps.why: Humiliates Serbia and Russia; Serbian nationalists turn to terror.

steps.name: First Balkan War
steps.what: Montenegro, then Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece attack the Ottoman Empire.
steps.why: Ottoman Europe shrinks to a corner of Thrace.

steps.name: Second Balkan War
steps.what: Bulgaria attacks its allies over Macedonia and loses.
steps.why: Serbia doubles in size and in confidence.

steps.name: Treaty of Bucharest
steps.what: Divides Macedonia between Serbia and Greece.
steps.why: The last border settlement before 1914.

stories.title: Steam, iron and railways
stories.blurb: Coal, steam and rail remake the continent from Lancashire outward; cities double, then double again.

steps.name: First railway locomotive
steps.what: Trevithick's engine hauls iron on the Penydarren tramroad.
steps.why: Steam can move on rails.

steps.name: Stockton and Darlington Railway
steps.what: The first public railway to use steam locomotives opens.
steps.why: Rail for coal becomes rail for everything.

steps.name: Liverpool and Manchester Railway
steps.what: The first intercity line with timetabled steam trains opens.
steps.why: The railway age begins.

steps.name: First railway on the continent
steps.what: Belgium opens Brussels–Mechelen, a state-planned network.
steps.why: Belgium becomes the continent's first industrial nation.

steps.name: Tsarskoye Selo Railway
steps.what: Russia's first public railway opens.
steps.why: A long lag: the Russian network grows fast only after 1860.

steps.name: First Italian railway
steps.what: Naples–Portici opens in the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
steps.why: Italy's divided states build divided networks.

steps.name: Corn Laws
steps.what: Britain abolishes tariffs on imported grain.
steps.why: Free trade becomes British doctrine.

steps.name: Great Exhibition
steps.what: The Crystal Palace shows the industry of all nations.
steps.why: Britain displays itself as workshop of the world.

steps.name: Bessemer process
steps.what: Henry Bessemer announces cheap mass steel-making.
steps.why: Cheap steel for rails, ships and guns.

steps.name: Cobden-Chevalier Treaty
steps.what: Britain and France cut tariffs.
steps.why: A web of trade treaties follows across Europe.

steps.name: London Underground opens
steps.what: The Metropolitan Railway opens the first underground line.
steps.why: Cities can grow outward on rails.

steps.name: Suez Canal opens
steps.what: The canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
steps.why: Europe to Asia in half the distance.

steps.name: Fréjus rail tunnel
steps.what: The first great Alpine tunnel opens.
steps.why: The Alps stop being a wall.

steps.name: Panic of 1873
steps.what: The Vienna stock exchange crashes.
steps.why: The "Long Depression" and a turn to protectionism.

steps.name: German protective tariff
steps.what: Bismarck's tariff on iron and grain.
steps.why: Europe turns away from free trade.

steps.name: Orient Express
steps.what: The first Orient Express leaves Paris for Constantinople.
steps.why: A continent you can cross in days.

steps.name: The automobile
steps.what: Karl Benz patents his motor car.
steps.why: The engine that will replace the horse.

steps.name: Trans-Siberian Railway begun
steps.what: Construction starts at the Pacific end.
steps.why: Russia binds Siberia to Europe by rail.

steps.name: Blériot flies the Channel
steps.what: Louis Blériot flies from near Calais to Dover in 37 minutes.
steps.why: Britain is no longer an island in the old sense; within five years aircraft go to war.

stories.title: People, ideas and rights
stories.blurb: Nationalism, liberalism, socialism, Darwin and the vote: the ideas that the century argued about.

steps.name: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
steps.what: Mary Wollstonecraft argues for women's education and equality.
steps.why: A founding text of feminism.
steps.wikipedia: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

steps.name: Addresses to the German Nation
steps.what: Fichte lectures on German national rebirth in French-occupied Berlin.
steps.why: Cultural nationalism becomes political.

steps.name: Beethoven's Ninth
steps.what: The Ninth Symphony premieres at the Kärntnertortheater.
steps.why: The Romantic hymn to brotherhood.

steps.name: On the Origin of Species
steps.what: Darwin publishes his theory of evolution by natural selection.
steps.why: Changes biology and unsettles religion.

steps.name: Emancipation of the serfs
steps.what: Alexander II frees some 23 million privately held serfs.
steps.why: The largest emancipation of the century, on terms that left peasants indebted.

steps.name: January Uprising
steps.what: Poles and Lithuanians rise against Russia.
steps.why: Crushed by 1864; Russification follows.

steps.name: Geneva Convention of 1864
steps.what: Twelve states agree to protect wounded soldiers and medics.
steps.why: The beginning of international humanitarian law.

steps.name: First International
steps.what: The International Workingmen's Association is founded.
steps.why: Socialism organises across borders.

steps.name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise
steps.what: The Habsburg monarchy becomes a dual state of Austria and Hungary.
steps.why: Buys peace with Hungary at the cost of the Slavs.

steps.name: Das Kapital
steps.what: Marx publishes the first volume.
steps.why: The theory behind the socialist parties.

steps.name: assassination of Alexander II of Russia
steps.what: Narodnaya Volya kills the tsar who freed the serfs.
steps.why: Reaction, and pogroms against Jews across the Pale.
steps.wikipedia: Assassination of Alexander II of Russia

steps.name: Social insurance
steps.what: Germany introduces compulsory health insurance; accident and pension laws follow.
steps.why: The first welfare state, built to undercut the socialists.

steps.name: Dreyfus affair
steps.what: A Jewish army captain is convicted of treason on forged evidence.
steps.why: Splits France; Herzl writes The Jewish State in 1896.

steps.name: First modern Olympics
steps.what: The revived Olympic Games open in Athens.
steps.why: Sport becomes international and national at once.

steps.name: The Interpretation of Dreams
steps.what: Freud publishes his theory of the unconscious (dated 1900).
steps.why: A new account of the mind.

steps.name: Bloody Sunday
steps.what: Troops fire on a peaceful petition march to the Winter Palace.
steps.why: Starts the 1905 Revolution; the tsar concedes a Duma.

steps.name: Special relativity
steps.what: Einstein, a patent clerk, publishes his annus mirabilis papers.
steps.why: Physics is rebuilt.

steps.name: Women vote in Finland
steps.what: Finland gives women the vote and the right to stand.
steps.why: The first in Europe; 19 women enter parliament in 1907.

stories.title: The road to 1914
stories.blurb: Alliances harden into two camps; a murder in Sarajevo sets them off in five weeks.

steps.name: League of the Three Emperors
steps.what: Germany, Austria-Hungary and Russia agree to consult.
steps.why: Bismarck's first system to isolate France.

steps.name: Dual Alliance
steps.what: Germany and Austria-Hungary sign a defensive alliance against Russia.
steps.why: The core of the Central Powers.

steps.name: Triple Alliance
steps.what: Italy joins Germany and Austria-Hungary.
steps.why: Bismarck's web is complete.

steps.name: Berlin Conference
steps.what: European powers set rules for claiming Africa.
steps.why: The Scramble for Africa is formalised.

steps.name: Bismarck dismissed
steps.what: William II forces out Bismarck; the Reinsurance Treaty with Russia lapses.
steps.why: Germany's new course frees Russia to look to France.

steps.name: Franco-Russian Alliance
steps.what: France and Russia ratify a military alliance.
steps.why: Germany faces a two-front war.

steps.name: German Naval Law
steps.what: Tirpitz's first law starts a battle fleet.
steps.why: The naval race turns Britain against Germany.

steps.name: Entente Cordiale
steps.what: Britain and France settle colonial quarrels.
steps.why: Old rivals become partners.

steps.name: First Moroccan Crisis
steps.what: William II lands in Tangier to challenge France.
steps.why: Backfires: Britain and France draw closer.

steps.name: HMS Dreadnought
steps.what: Britain launches an all-big-gun battleship.
steps.why: Every older battleship is obsolete; the race restarts.

steps.name: Anglo-Russian Convention
steps.what: Britain and Russia settle Persia, Afghanistan and Tibet.
steps.why: The Triple Entente is formed.

steps.name: Agadir Crisis
steps.what: A German gunboat arrives at Agadir.
steps.why: Britain signals it would stand by France.

steps.name: assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
steps.what: Gavrilo Princip shoots the Austrian heir and his wife.
steps.why: The spark of the First World War.

steps.name: The blank cheque
steps.what: Germany promises Austria-Hungary unconditional support.
steps.why: Turns a Balkan quarrel into a European war.

steps.name: Austria-Hungary declares war on Serbia
steps.what: After an ultimatum Serbia could not fully accept.
steps.why: Russia mobilises; the alliances engage.

steps.name: Germany declares war on Russia
steps.what: Then on France on 3 August.
steps.why: The Schlieffen Plan runs through Belgium.

steps.name: Britain declares war on Germany
steps.what: After Germany invades neutral Belgium.
steps.why: A world war: the long nineteenth century ends.
steps.wikipedia: British entry into World War I
